To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the hierarchical structures of language and music are not comparable at the syntactic level, (2) the hierarchical structures that are found in both domains are comparable at the level of action planning, and (3) the hierarchical structures in language arise in the conceptual domain and in music arise in the affective-gesture and socio-intentional domains.
music and language are different but similar in the sense that both are systems of hierarchical structures that are used for action planning and that are processed in time.

the syntax of music and language are similar in that both are hierarchical action planning structures, whereas they differ in that the hierarchical action structures of music are more strongly related to affective-gestures and socio-intentional systems than the hierarchical action structures in language, and in that the hierarchical structures of language are more strongly related than those of music to the conceptual system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way syntax can be investigated in language and music, and how the grammar of action can be used to bring the two domains closer to each other.
a new perspective on the syntax of music and language that is based on an action-oriented approach.

the syntax of music and language are similar at the level of hierarchical structures of actions and their sequential integration, but they are different at the level of the goal of action.

the grammar of action provides a new way of comparing music and language, and a new way to understand the role of hierarchical structure building in both domains.
